title: Singapore Omnichannel Fulfilment Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily order activity at the 40 fulfilment nodes of Sagaseed Retail, a fictional Singapore omnichannel retailer, into on-time fulfilment and disruption KPIs, 7-day fulfilment-disruption risk scores, order-to-ready time anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: On-time fulfilment rate, late orders, fulfilment disruption hours and net sales in SGD for 40 fulfilment nodes across Jurong East, Tampines, Woodlands, Ang Mo Kio and Punggol.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to node-day rows.
The disruption-cause chart shows which causes cost the most hours: the two area-wide mega-sale order surges in Tampines and Jurong East lead, then packing station outages.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of omnichannel KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which nodes should the fulfilment network team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each node's probability of a fulfilment disruption in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 labelled days, against the base rate; precision is above the base rate, recall is low, so treat scores as triage.
Anomaly detection flags order-to-ready time outliers per node, and the forecast projects network-wide late orders for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are cycle counts and staff training keeping up?

talking_points: Cycle count on-time rate, staff training coverage and pending trainings frame the store-side gaps.
Cycle count on-time rate against disruption hours by node shows where overdue counts and disruptions move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, node, disruption-cause and risk tables only.
show: Cycle count on-time rate and training coverage
Cycle count on-time rate vs disruption hours
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when an order misses its promised time right now?

talking_points: Live order fulfilment events land in RAW.LIVE_ORDERS, from the Snowflake-native simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs LATE orders with an SOP hint and the node's current risk band, then emails the on-call fulfilment lead.
tabs.call_out: From a late order to an incident in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 18 synthetic fulfilment disruption SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
